merged_guidance.title: Order complete display frames by the current protocol's arrival identity
merged_guidance.applicability: Packets decode to complete replacement frames, completions may reverse reception order, and the current task or protocol explicitly defines display freshness by packet arrival within a logical display owner.
merged_guidance.event_relation: Assign reception identity before decoding. Publish only an eligible frame newer than the owner's published order, committing that watermark before callback-capable painting. Determine visit-local, attempt-local and cross-retry scope from the current protocol; resetting a scope must not admit stale attempt results.
merged_guidance.preservation: Preserve each independently required audit effect even for a frame suppressed from display. Later legitimate values may decrease or reset. Respect owner eligibility as well as order, including during reentrant publication.
merged_guidance.exclusion: Loaded bytes, completion time and numeric monotonicity are not arrival identity. Do not drop required delta events. If the source defines server revisions or a different ordering policy, use that policy rather than importing arrival order.
merged_guidance.verification: Reverse decode completion; let the later-received frame have a lower value; emit or finish another frame synchronously while painting. Verify no rollback, retained audits, and correct ordering scope across retry, navigation and same-source reopening.

record.title: Publish competing results using the contract-defined version order
record.applicability: Complete replacement frames compete within the same logical display owner; the current task defines freshness by packet arrival order.
record.event_relation: Assign arrival identity before decoding. Publish a completion only if it is newer than the last displayed frame for that logical owner, committing freshness state before callback-capable painting.
record.preservation: Preserve separately required auditing of admitted frames, and allow legitimate decreases or resets in business values.
record.exclusion: Do not compare loaded bytes as a version. Do not discard required delta events. If the current protocol defines server revisions or ordering across attempts, use that protocol and owner scope instead.
record.verification: Reverse decode completion, include decreasing full-frame values, exercise painting reentry and verify the version scope across retry and reopening.

record.title: Prevent full-frame rollback using arrival versions
record.applicability: Packets decode to complete replacement frames, completion may reverse arrival order, and the current protocol defines freshness by arrival.
record.event_relation: Assign arrival order before decoding. Paint only frames newer than the display owner's published order. Commit that order before invoking a paint callback that may reenter.
record.preservation: Older frames cannot overwrite newer display, but admitted audit effects remain under their contract. Later loaded values may decrease or reset.
record.exclusion: Do not compare byte counts to determine freshness. Historical cases describe both attempt-local and visit-local ordering; determine the cross-retry scope from the current protocol. Resetting order must not admit stale attempt results. Do not apply full-frame dropping to required delta events.
record.verification: Reverse decode completion, decrease the newer frame's value and emit another packet synchronously during painting. Check version scope across retry and visit replacement.

obligation_checklist: Only with target-supported full-frame arrival-order policy; never required deltas.
Preserve independent audit and decreases/resets; commit watermark before callbacks.
Determine visit/attempt scope from current source.
scope: User-authorized source-preserving consolidation; source quotations are historical evidence, not requirements for a new task. No new model evaluation or effectiveness claim.
